title: The heart
examples: How does the heart pump blood to the body?
What happens when the heart beats?
What is the difference between the atria and ventricles?

explain.say: The human heart has four chambers. These chambers are the rooms where blood collects and is pumped.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the human heart. Look at the right atrium, the right ventricle and the left atrium. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The atria are the upper chambers. They receive blood coming into the heart from the body and lungs.
The ventricles are the lower chambers. They pump blood out of the heart to the body or lungs.
Valves keep blood flowing in one direction only. They open and close to prevent backflow.
The cardiac cycle describes the full sequence of heart actions. It includes atrial contraction and ventricular contraction.
Cardiac output is the total volume of blood pumped per minute. It is calculated by heart rate times stroke volume.

faq.q: What is the main job of the heart?
faq.a: The heart pumps blood around the body to deliver oxygen and nutrients. It keeps the circulatory system moving continuously.
asks: How does blood get around my body?
What does the heart do for me?

faq.q: What is the difference between the atria and ventricles?
faq.a: The atria receive blood first, and the ventricles are the powerful pumps that push blood out to the body.
asks: Which chambers are the receiving rooms?

faq.q: Why are the valves so important?
faq.a: The valves act like one-way doors, ensuring that blood only moves forward through the circuit. This prevents blood from flowing backward.
asks: What stops blood from going backward?
Do the valves let blood go both ways?

faq.a: It measures the total amount of blood the heart pumps every single minute. It is a measure of the heart's overall pumping efficiency.
asks: How much blood is pumped per minute?
What is the total blood volume pumped?

faq.q: What causes the heart to beat?
faq.a: The heart beats due to electrical impulses that spread through the heart muscle tissue. This electrical signal triggers the muscle to contract.
asks: Is the heart controlled by electricity?

facts: The heart is a muscular organ located in the chest.
Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium.
Oxygenated blood leaves the left ventricle to the body.
The heart beats rhythmically throughout life.

quiz.say: If the heart rate is sixty beats per minute and the stroke volume is sixty milliliters, what is the cardiac output?
quiz.why: Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume, so sixty times sixty is three thousand six hundred.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you only used one of the measurements given in the problem.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you multiplied sixty by six, forgetting the unit for volume.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you must multiply the two values together, not divide them.

quiz.say: Which chamber receives oxygenated blood returning from the lungs?
quiz.show: Oxygenated blood enters the Left Atrium
quiz.why: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, which connect to the lungs.

wrong.0: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood out, it does not receive it first.
wrong.1: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
wrong.3: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood returning from the body.

quiz.say: If a person has a heart rate of 72 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 milliliters, what is the cardiac output?
quiz.why: You multiply the heart rate by the stroke volume: seventy-two multiplied by seventy equals five thousand forty.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you added the heart rate to the stroke volume.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you only used the heart rate and ignored the stroke volume.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you added the two numbers together instead of multiplying them.
